chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Mansur Al-Sayqal, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Hajj with us is upon three types: a Mutamatti' pilgrim, and a Mufrid pilgrim who brings the sacrifice, and a Mufrid pilgrim for Hajj.'

key_terms.سَائِقٌ لِلْهَدْيِ: Saqiq lil-hady (one who brings/ushers the sacrificial animal)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٌ: Mutamatti' (one who performs Umrah and Hajj separately, combining them)
key_terms.مُفْرِدٌ: Mufrid (one who performs Hajj or Umrah exclusively)

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of Hajj in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the three canonical forms of Hajj—Tamattu', Qiran, and Ifrad—emphasizing the ritual distinction between those who combine Umrah and Hajj with a sacrifice and those who perform them separately. This hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the presence of the sacrificial animal (Hady) is the defining marker of the Qiran type, distinguishing it from the Ifrad pilgrim who performs Hajj alone. This classification remains foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the specific rites and exemptions applicable to each pilgrim.
